patterns_data.top_pattern: ME authorized acute hospital admissions surged in HMO
patterns_data.pattern_details: ME HMO inpatient acute hospital spend rose sharply because authorized admissions increased, not because payment per admission increased. Admissions were up substantially while paid per admit fell, which means the cost problem is fundamentally one of more hospital use. This is the single largest business pattern in the file and should be treated as a utilization-management priority.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A large spend increase driven by more authorized inpatient use will not be fixed through unit-price action alone.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a focused ME inpatient utilization review for HMO acute hospital admissions with PA required, including admission appropriateness, length-of-stay management, and discharge planning.
evidence_summary: ME HMO acute hospital spend increased by about $26.0M.
Admissions increased by 676 and claims increased by 352.
Average paid per admit fell by about $35.0K, confirming the increase was volume-driven rather than unit-cost-driven.
This one pattern accounts for about 85% of the positive change tied to its source evidence.

patterns_data.top_pattern: CT and GA acute hospital spend is concentrated in a few high-cost providers
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: CT PPO and GA HMO / ACUTE HOSPITAL
key_driver_codes: Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: In CT and GA, acute hospital cost growth is heavily concentrated in a small number of hospitals rather than spread broadly across the market. Yale New Haven, Wellstar MCG Health Medical Center, and Emory Saint Joseph's Hospital together drive most of the increase, with both more admissions and higher paid per admit in key cases. This is a provider economics issue as much as a utilization issue, so contracting and UM need to work together.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: When a few providers account for most of the increase, targeted contract and care-management action can materially change the trend.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a joint network and UM action plan for Yale New Haven, Wellstar MCG, and Emory Saint Joseph's Hospital, focused on authorized acute admissions, neurosurgical severity, chemotherapy episodes, and reimbursement guardrails.
evidence_summary: YALE NEW HAVEN HOSPITAL added about $19.7M, with 258 more admissions and roughly +$6.2K paid per admit.
WELLSTAR MCG HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER added about $7.7M, with 50 more admissions and about +$80.6K paid per admit.
EMORY SAINT JOSEPH'S HOSPITAL added about $5.4M, with 174 more admissions and about +$5.2K paid per admit.
A smaller GA non-auth acute hospital craniotomy signal added about $124K on higher unit cost despite lower volume.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Auth-code shifts and not-mapped facilities are obscuring the true story in several states
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Authorization coding and facility mapping in CT, GA, CA / CO / ME / WI, ME, CA, and IN
patterns_data.pattern_details: A meaningful share of the observed change sits in authorization-code movement and unmapped facility values rather than clean business categories. CT and GA alone show large auth-code distribution shifts, and several states also carry spend in Not Mapped facility buckets. These issues should be treated as gating validation work before drawing firm conclusions on authorization performance or provider action.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If authorization or facility mapping moved, the business may target the wrong market, provider, or policy lever.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Reconcile authorization-code assignment and facility mapping for the named states and providers, then rerun downstream UM and reimbursement actions only on validated populations.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Source groups explicitly flag auth or mapping shifts and require validation before action; several additional groups carry unmapped facility values.
evidence_summary: CT auth-code distribution shifts contributed about $11.5M, centered on YALE NEW HAVEN HOSPITAL.
GA auth-code distribution shifts contributed about $6.4M, led by WELLSTAR MCG HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER and EMORY SAINT JOSEPH'S HOSPITAL.
CA / CO / ME / WI show another roughly $3.3M of gross auth-code movement, including a -$1.7M swing in ME.
Not Mapped facility values add about $2.7M across ME, CT, CA, and IN.

patterns_data.pattern_details: After the biggest state and provider spikes are removed, there is still a sizable acute hospital trend spread across HMO, EPO, POS, and PPO products. The recurring themes are more admissions and higher-paid low-frequency surgical or oncology-related cases, especially craniotomy episodes. This is a broad inpatient management issue that needs standard guardrails across markets, not a one-off fix.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A wide residual inpatient trend can keep eroding performance even after the top provider issues are addressed.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Apply a cross-market inpatient review on acute hospital admissions across HMO, EPO, POS, and PPO books, prioritizing craniotomy and other high-paid low-volume admits for medical necessity, level of care, and contract adequacy review.
evidence_summary: The multi-state HMO acute hospital segment added about $9.0M.
Within that segment, CO craniotomy cases added about $1.9M and CA EPO acute hospital craniotomy utilization added about $856K.
MO EPO acute hospital cases added about $441K, largely from craniotomy.
IN / TX POS acute hospital cases added about $264K, again led by high-cost surgical episodes.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Post-acute, pediatric, and behavioral facilities are pulling more spend outside core acute hospitals
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Physical Rehab, SNF - FREE STANDING, LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL, CHILDRENS, CRITICAL ACCESS, ACUTE PSYCH, NF
key_driver_codes: Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: A meaningful secondary trend is building outside standard acute hospitals, especially in rehab, SNF, LTCH, children's, critical access, and behavioral settings. GA behavioral facilities stand out, while musculoskeletal aftercare and rehab patterns appear across CA, TX, VA, OH, MO, and CT. The business lever here is site-of-care management, post-acute steering, and behavioral network control rather than broad inpatient acute hospital action.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: These settings can grow quietly across many small segments and become persistent spend leakage if steerage and prior authorization rules are weak.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review post-acute and behavioral site-of-care pathways, authorization rules, and network steerage for rehab, SNF, LTCH, children's, critical access, and psych facilities, starting with GA behavioral providers and CA/TX rehab activity.
evidence_summary: GA HMO acute psych utilization added about $594K, driven mainly by LAKEVIEW BEHAVIORAL HEALTH and GREENLEAF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH HOSPITAL.
CA EPO Physical Rehab added about $503K, and TX HMO Physical Rehab added about $269K.
GA behavioral Psychoses case-mix patterns add roughly $447K across new, recurring, and mixed behavioral episodes.
CA musculoskeletal aftercare and related non-acute patterns contribute more than $1.0M across SNF, NF, and other aftercare settings.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic Med/Surg cases are creating outsized spikes
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: GA / UNATTRIBUTED, GA, and CO / IP Med/Surg
key_driver_codes: ECMO or Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck with Major O.R. Procedures
Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck without Major O.R. Procedures
Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Cardiac Valve and Other Major Cardiothoracic Procedures without Cardiac Catheterization with MCC
Other Major Cardiovascular Procedures with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: This is a classic rare-catastrophic pattern: very small numbers of exceptionally expensive Med/Surg cases are producing large spend spikes. The drivers include ECMO or tracheostomy, complex craniotomy, and major cardiothoracic or cardiovascular procedures, often with only one or two incremental admits. These cases need case-level review and financial protection planning rather than broad utilization intervention.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A handful of catastrophic cases can distort trend, trigger stop-loss exposure, and require very different action than routine inpatient growth.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Perform case-level clinical and billing review for catastrophic surgical admissions, confirm pricing and contract terms for ECMO, trach, craniotomy, and cardiothoracic cases, and assess stop-loss or outlier payment protection.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Several drivers are single-case or two-admission outliers, and one source segment includes UNATTRIBUTED volume.
evidence_summary: GA / UNATTRIBUTED ECMO or tracheostomy-related outliers added about $4.9M, including a WELLSTAR MCG HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER case worth about $2.9M.
GA new high-cost cardiovascular and trach-related Med/Surg cases added about $4.9M.
CO craniotomy-related volume and intensity added about $4.2M, and separate rare high-cost neuro cases added about $3.0M.
Many of these signals come from only 2 to 14 added admissions, with paid per admit often increasing by tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: CA / CT / GA, WI, and CA / IP Med/Surg and ACUTE HOSPITAL
key_driver_codes: Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-cell and Other Immunotherapies
Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Oncology-related inpatient spend is showing up as a separate business issue, not just as noise inside general acute hospital trend. The biggest signals are CAR-T and other immunotherapies at Yale New Haven, inpatient chemotherapy growth in WI, and smaller chemo-related acute hospital pressure in CA. These episodes typically require separate clinical policy, case management, and reimbursement treatment from standard Med/Surg admissions.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: High-cost oncology episodes can grow quickly and are governed by different medical policy and contract levers than routine inpatient care.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Trigger an oncology episode review for CAR-T and inpatient chemotherapy admissions, including medical policy adherence, site appropriateness, and reimbursement adequacy for these therapies.
evidence_summary: YALE NEW HAVEN HOSPITAL CAR-T and immunotherapy activity added about $2.6M.
WI inpatient chemotherapy added about $1.6M, with 52 more admissions and roughly +$10.5K paid per admit.
CA EPO acute hospital chemotherapy added about $300K.
The pattern combines both more oncology admissions and higher-intensity oncology episodes.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Maternity and women's surgical episodes are rising in TX and adding acute hospital pressure elsewhere
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: TX, GA, CT, CA / IP OB Dlvry/Well NB and ACUTE HOSPITAL
key_driver_codes: Vaginal Delivery without Sterilization or D&C with CC
Uterine and Adnexa Procedures for Nonmalignancy without CC/MCC
PTL 3RD TRI W/PT DEL 3RD TRI NA/UNS
patterns_data.pattern_details: TX is showing a meaningful maternity complexity pattern in inpatient delivery episodes, while CT, CA, GA, VA, KY, and OH also show added acute hospital spend in vaginal delivery or uterine/adnexa surgery. The TX signals point to both higher-complexity deliveries and more delivery volume, while the non-TX groups suggest broader women's health surgical pressure. This should be handled as an OB and women's health pathway issue, not folded into general inpatient management.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Maternity and women's surgical trends require different clinical pathways, provider engagement, and avoidable-admission controls than general Med/Surg.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run an OB and women's health review on delivery complications and uterine procedure pathways, including provider practice patterns, admission thresholds, and reimbursement consistency.
evidence_summary: TX maternity-focused clinical groups contributed about $1.6M across gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, preterm labor, and post-term pregnancy.
CT PPO vaginal delivery utilization added about $575K, with 50 more admissions.
GA women's surgical case mix added about $392K, led by intramural leiomyoma of uterus.
A separate CA / CT / GA HMO acute hospital utilization pattern added about $523K and CA / KY / OH PPO acute hospital women's surgery added about $118K.
